summary: One change: the RDS master username on aws_db_instance.orders goes from orders_admin to orders_owner. Changing the master username forces replacement of the instance, which POLICY.md rule 2 forbids in a normal PR. deletion_protection and a final snapshot are set, so the apply would probably be blocked or fail rather than silently destroy data. The PR still needs a migration plan. The scanners reported no findings.

findings.title: RDS master username change forces DB replacement
findings.why_it_matters: Changing `username` on aws_db_instance.orders is a force-new attribute, so the plan replaces the stateful orders database. POLICY.md rule 2 forbids replacing aws_db_instance in a normal PR. deletion_protection and the final snapshot reduce the risk of data loss but do not make the replacement acceptable.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert the username change to keep the existing instance. If the rename is really needed, do it as a planned migration: snapshot and restore or use DMS into a new instance, with explicit approval. Do not change the master username in place.
